name: Juse
description: Juse is a unique and high-intensity 'competitive patience' game from Sri Lanka. Unlike traditional solitaire, several players compete in real-time to build piles in the center and on each other's discard piles. It is a game of rapid pattern recognition where failure to play a 'forced' card results in a penalty (Juse!), making it a chaotic and energetic social experience.

history.origins: Developed in Sri Lanka as a local adaptation of games like 'Crapette' or 'Racing Demon'. The name 'Juse' (possibly a variant of the name 'Joseph' or a local exclamation) refers to the act of calling out a player's mistake.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Becomes a popular social game in Sri Lankan homes and schools.
1990s: Rules are documented and standardized for club play.
Present: A beloved traditional game, specifically known for the 'Juse!' penalty call.
history.cultural: In Sri Lankan culture, Juse is a game of loud exclamations and sharp focus; calling 'Juse' on a friend is the highlight of the social interaction.
history.evolution: The game evolved to be cyclic (Ace follows King), which prevents the game from 'stalling' like many other solitaire variants.

setup.players: Any number, but odd numbers (3, 5, 7) are traditional.
setup.dealing: Deal cards face-down equally until 1 card remains. That last card is placed in the center to start the first foundation pile.

rules.objective: Be the first to empty both your draw pile and your discard pile.
rules.gameplay:
1. Each player has a face-down draw pile and a face-up discard pile.
2. In the center, four foundation piles (one for each suit) are built UPWARDS in suit.
3. **Turn Action**: You must play cards from your draw/discard pile to the center OR onto an opponent's discard pile (if one rank higher, regardless of suit).
4. **Forced Play**: If a card CAN be played to a center foundation, it MUST be played before any other move.
5. **Juse!**: If a player misses a forced play, any other player can shout 'JUSE!'. The offender must take cards from the bottom of every other player's pile.

strategy.basic: Keep a very close eye on the center foundations. The moment a rank appears that you have on your discard pile, play it immediately. Speed is everything.
strategy.intermediate: Offensive Filling: Use every opportunity to dump your cards onto your opponents' discard piles. This 'buries' their useful cards and gets you closer to winning.
strategy.advanced: Trap Playing: If you have a card that could go to the center, but playing it would help your opponent more than you (e.g., they have the next card in sequence), try to delayâ€”but be careful not to get 'Juse'd'!
tips: Always check the center foundations before looking at your own draw pile.
If you are about to play a card on an opponent, check if it could go to the center first. Foundation play is always priority.

scoring.description: No points; the first player to empty both their draw pile and discard pile wins the game.
scoring.winCondition: Be the first to get rid of your last card so that both your draw pile and your discard pile are empty.
